TCS-0023: Remove the retired pointer already consolidated into TCS-6543 by its completed review. Wigderson Open Problem 17.9 concerns growing-support juntas, not the inherited DNF label. Its weaker milestone and original bibliography are preserved on TCS-6543; no equivalence to the stronger full junta target is asserted.
TCS-0485: Exact duplicate of TCS-0310 according to the completed source review: Dagstuhl report 10.4230/DagRep.14.1.49, section 6.1, points to the same Monet weighted-unambiguous-DNF question (https://cstheory.stackexchange.com/questions/53733). All three source references are already on TCS-0310.
TCS-0520: The completed card review already resolves the specified promise-free constant-online versus linear-dynamic LCL separation negatively. Its explicit simulation composition yields deterministic O(sqrt(n) polylog(n)) LOCAL and dynamic locality. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01903v4, Lemma 7.5; https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05191v2, section 4.1, Corollary 4.13 and Appendix A; ICALP 2023.10 model simulations. This cleanup relies on that recorded review, not a new proof audit.
TCS-0521: The completed card review already resolves the specified promise-free constant-dynamic versus linear-LOCAL LCL separation negatively: dynamic O(1) implies online O(1), then deterministic O(sqrt(n) polylog(n)) LOCAL. Sources: ICALP 2023.10; https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01903v4, Lemma 7.5; https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05191v2, section 4.1 and Appendix A. This cleanup accepts the recorded simulation derivation without repeating full review.
TCS-6579: Remove the scalar Crouzeix inequality already marked resolved in its completed review. The saved review cites Jin, The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set (https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202607.1919/v4), Lorist-Schwenninger (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03841v2), and the explicit Townsend-Greenbaum expert assessment (https://alextownsend.net/essays/SIAMNews_CrouzeixConjecture.pdf). Journal peer review remained pending; no independent formalization audit is claimed. The complete matrix-valued conjecture is a distinct target.
TCS-2711: The literal o(2^k n |P|) pairwise fault-tolerant reachability-preserver question is answered affirmatively by its own source, Chakraborty-Chatterjee-Choudhary, ICALP 2022.35 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2022.35), abstract final contribution and the selected page-14 passage. The exact optimal-size frontier is a separate question.
TCS-3503: The historical superlinear-size obstruction for two-hop unit-disk spanners is false: Conroy-Toth, SoCG 2022.30 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.SoCG.2022.30), proves O(n)-edge two-hop spanners for every n-vertex unit-disk graph. This settles the ISAAC 2020.57 question. TCS-2932 concerns arbitrary disks or rectangles and is retained.
TCS-3515: Extracted introductory motivation answered within the source model: Chan-Chung-Lin-Shi, ITCS 2020.75 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2020.75), gives the secure MPC compiler under compact FHE and its stated cryptographic assumptions, preserving rounds and allowing the specified security-parameter space overhead with fewer than one third corrupted machines. It is not a remaining open question in that model, nor an unconditional cryptographic existence theorem.
TCS-3390: The literal question whether additional interaction rounds can reduce sample/comparison complexity is answered by Gopi et al., Locally Private Hypothesis Selection (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v125/gopi20a.html). The source supplies round-dependent algorithms and near-matching lower bounds, including O(log log k)-round nearly linear sample complexity. Removing the historical improvement question does not assert every constant or quantitative refinement is settled.
TCS-5052: The source itself resolves the last-iterate logarithmic-factor question for its standard nonsmooth gradient-descent schedules: Harvey-Liaw-Plan-Randhawa (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v99/harvey19a.html) gives matching O(log(T)/T) and Omega(log(T)/T) bounds, including a deterministic lower-bound example. Other step-size conventions are outside this deletion reason.
TCS-5148: Historical bounded learner-to-compression existence question, already answered in the binary finite-VC setting discussed by Hanneke-Kontorovich-Sadigurschi (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v98/hanneke19a.html). That source explicitly builds on Moran-Yehudayoff and extends efficient conversion to approximate real-valued reconstruction. The stronger linear-in-VC compression-size conjecture is not being removed.
TCS-5346: The source answers its own introductory DFS streaming question. Khan-Mehta, Depth First Search in the Semi-Streaming Model, STACS 2019.42 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.STACS.2019.42), supplies the sublinear-pass/sublinear-in-m-space tradeoff quoted as missing in the historical motivation; the paper abstract explicitly identifies this as its contribution.
TCS-5441: The extracted 2014 statement concerns classification of finite-domain non-Boolean CSPs, not the universal-factor-graph theorem in the title. The finite-domain dichotomy was established independently by Bulatov and Zhuk in 2017. Bulatov, A dichotomy theorem for nonuniform CSPs, Theorem 1.1 (https://www2.cs.sfu.ca/~abulatov/papers/dichotomy.pdf), gives precisely polynomial-time solvability or NP-completeness for every finite constraint language on a finite domain. Infinite-domain and promise CSP questions remain distinct.
TCS-6002: The selected historical passage states the finite-domain Feder-Vardi dichotomy, settled independently by Bulatov and Zhuk in 2017. See Bulatov, A dichotomy theorem for nonuniform CSPs, Theorem 1.1 (https://www2.cs.sfu.ca/~abulatov/papers/dichotomy.pdf). The temporal/infinite-domain subject of the containing paper does not turn this particular finite-domain quotation into a remaining open question.
TCS-5641: The historical complexity question for optimal Stack Rearrangement is classified as NP-hard by the containing source itself: Geft, Hardness of Multi-Agent Path Finding on Trees: A Unified Approach, ESA 2026.159 (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.ESA.2026.159). Its abstract explicitly reports the Stack Rearrangement hardness result used for the tree-motion reductions. This records the proved hardness classification, without claiming P differs from NP.
TCS-5968: The introductory product-depth-two set-multilinear lower-bound milestone is achieved in the same paper: Kush-Saraf, CCC 2022.38 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2022.38; https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00611), gives n^{Omega(n^{1/Delta})} for an explicit degree-n Nisan-Wigderson polynomial. At fixed product depth two, circuit unfolding costs a polynomial factor, so the stated formula theorem supplies the requested circuit lower-bound scale. Stronger general-formula or IMM-specific targets are separate.
TCS-6830: The Natarajan-dimension-only realizable multiclass sample bound is refuted by Brukhim-Carmon-Dinur-Moran-Yehudayoff, A Characterization of Multiclass Learnability, FOCS 2022 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01550; DOI 10.1109/FOCS54457.2022.00093). Their classes have Natarajan dimension one and arbitrarily large DS dimension, precluding a label-count-independent bound of the saved textbook form. DS dimension, rather than Natarajan dimension alone, characterizes general learnability.
TCS-6886: The 2010 survey Open Problem 6 asking for superpolynomial depth-four arithmetic-circuit lower bounds outside characteristic two is settled by later low-depth circuit lower bounds. Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas established characteristic-zero/large-characteristic bounds (FOCS 2021); Forbes extended them to every field in CCC 2024.31 (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.31). The stronger exponential lower-bound question is retained.
TCS-6891: The 2010 survey Open Problem 11 asking for superpolynomial Sigma-Pi-Sigma circuit lower bounds over infinite fields is settled by general low-depth arithmetic-circuit lower bounds: Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas, FOCS 2021 (https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2021/081/), and the all-field extension of Forbes, CCC 2024.31 (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.31). This is the saved superpolynomial milestone, not an exponential or unrestricted-depth lower bound.
TCS-7142: The saved Geelen conjecture is proved by James Davies, Vertex-minor-closed classes are chi-bounded (https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05069v3). Every proper vertex-minor-closed class is chi-bounded, including the class excluding any fixed vertex-minor. Polynomial chi-bounds and related algorithmic refinements are not asserted here.
TCS-0435: The source report itself closes the ordinary-persistence subcubic representative-computation question: Dagstuhl Seminar 24092, section 4.1, printed pp. 222-223 (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/04dagstuhl-reports/volume14/issue02/DagRep.14.2/DagRep.14.2.pdf#page=224). The proposer reports that the cited algorithm computes ordinary representatives in matrix-multiplication time. The same update explicitly keeps subcubic zigzag representatives open; that is not the literal ordinary-persistence target removed here.
TCS-5139: The extracted motivation is answered in the containing Phoenix paper, Damgard-Escudero-Polychroniadou, ITC 2023.7 (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2023.7). It constructs protocols for temporary adversarial dropouts and comebacks and proves optimal honest-online overlap requirements for perfect, statistical and computational security. Termination retains the stated availability assumptions; the result does not promise termination with unrestricted permanent absence.
TCS-4891: Duplicate of TCS-0677: both represent Blanc-Lange-Qiao-Tan, COLT 2022, Open Problem 1 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/open-problem-blanc22a.html), asking for poly(n,s,1/epsilon)-time proper decision-tree learning with membership queries under the uniform distribution. The precise source formulation and locator have been transferred to TCS-0677 before removal.
